record.file_problem: The article is present, but the supplied text does not include the numeric contents of the referenced tables and figures; only values stated in the prose can be recorded.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses the difference-in-means extraction and steering approach associated with the original work, but applies it to narrativity, persona, harm, and evaluation-awareness directions rather than testing the refusal direction itself.
record.gate_note: The study measures jailbreak ASR under steering of other directions. Those results do not test whether the refusal direction is suppressed by jailbreaks or whether ablating it removes refusal. The story-direction ASR results are recorded as related findings that fit none of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study applies the difference-in-means recipe of Arditi et al. to extract and steer story, persona, harm and eval-awareness directions on jailbreak prompts. It never extracts, ablates or adds the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, and it never measures whether jailbreaks suppress that direction. Its ASR results concern other constructs, so they bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Authors conclude a narrativity direction distinct from persona, harm and eval directions causally moves jailbreak ASR in both models, mainly through loss of specificity rather than explicit refusal. They do not test the refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means directions and residual-stream steering, but extracts narrativity and other framing or request properties rather than a refusal direction; steering is at selected single layers rather than an all-layer refusal-direction ablation. This is a research post, not a reproduction of the original refusal-direction experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The story layer chosen by the fictional/non-fictional probe gap produced much larger ASR effects than the layer chosen by Cohen's d: the text reports a 4× difference in Qwen and a 12× difference in Gemma. Outcomes also vary by model and steering direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtracting a story direction lowers jailbreak ASR (Qwen −50.8 pts, Gemma −73) and adding it raises ASR (+14.1, +29). The drop comes from vague, non-specific answers rather than explicit refusals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A narrativity direction causally affects jailbreak success, largely via answer specificity rather than refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering the persona direction at L15 in Qwen moves ASR by −98.4 (restore) and +62.8 (suppress). The harm component of the persona direction alone recovers 93% of the restore effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona and harm directions extracted by difference-in-means modulate jailbreak refusal, and persona's effect is largely carried by its harm component.

record.problems: The authors note that there was no random direction control at matched steering strength, not every layer was swept, and steering attribution was performed at selected layers. The study tests only two models. It does not evaluate broad capability preservation.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were entered: comparisons and effects for persona, harm, and evaluation-awareness directions concern those separate directions rather than the refusal direction or a listed claim version. Referenced table and figure cells whose numeric values are absent from the supplied text were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: No refusal-direction ablation or addition, and no capability check.
Does not test whether jailbreaks (fictional or other) suppress the refusal direction, and does no adversarial training.
A harm direction is steered, but its separation from a refusal direction is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited only as the source of the extraction recipe. The persona and harm steering results are stated in prose but were left out of the rows, which is defensible because they bear on no version. All four rows are correctly linked to 'none'.

versions.untested_parts: Does not intervene on the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, test its addition or ablation, or assess preservation of general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Comparing other directions and their steering effects does not test whether refusal itself is encoded by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Does not test transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Does not vary refusal training or test how training determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.
